statements.impact_statement: CVE-2020-8911 (GHSA-f5pg-7wfw-84q9, GO-2022-0646): the V1 Amazon S3 encryption client in github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go (package service/s3/s3crypto) lets callers encrypt objects with AES-CBC without a message authentication code, so an attacker with write access to the bucket who can observe whether a client with the key fails to decrypt an object can recover its plaintext through a padding oracle. AWS addressed it in V2 of the S3 encryption client API, which no longer encrypts new objects with CBC: EncryptionClientV2 and DecryptionClientV2 were added in aws-sdk-go 1.33.0 by pull request 3403, and the GitHub advisory gives 1.34.0 as the first patched version. The V1 clients remain in the module, and the Go vulnerability entry lists every aws-sdk-go version, with no fixed version, and the functions s3crypto.NewDecryptionClient and s3crypto.NewEncryptionClient. Sources: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f5pg-7wfw-84q9, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2022-0646, https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/pull/3403. We checked every published opentelemetry-collector-contrib-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 22 builds, 0.156.0-r0 to the current 0.165.0-r2, on x86_64 and aarch64 (44 packages), each against its index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/otelcol-contrib, a statically linked Go program (no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies) built with CGO_ENABLED=0. Its Go build information lists github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go v1.55.8, with no replace directive, in every build. No build links the S3 encryption client: the Go function table of every build, which lists runtime.main as a control, has no function from github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/service/s3/s3crypto, so neither NewDecryptionClient nor NewEncryptionClient is present, and a byte search of the program in every build, which also catches the names of inlined functions, finds no aws-sdk-go/service/s3/s3crypto. name, while it finds aws-sdk-go/aws. names in every build. The same function-table reader and byte search find s3crypto.NewDecryptionClient and s3crypto.NewEncryptionClient in test programs we built with aws-sdk-go 1.55.8 for amd64 and arm64. The vulnerable code is not in this package.

Read every published alloy-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository, 1.18.1-0 to 1.22.0-16, on amd64 and arm64 (1.21.2-0 was published for arm64 only); 87 packages, with no debug-symbol packages published for this source. CVE-2020-8911 (GHSA-f5pg-7wfw-84q9, GO-2022-0646): the V1 Amazon S3 encryption client in github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go (package service/s3/s3crypto) lets callers encrypt objects with AES-CBC without a message authentication code, so an attacker with write access to the bucket who can observe whether a client with the key fails to decrypt an object can recover its plaintext through a padding oracle. AWS addressed it in V2 of the S3 encryption client API, which no longer encrypts new objects with CBC: EncryptionClientV2 and DecryptionClientV2 were added in aws-sdk-go 1.33.0 by pull request 3403, and the GitHub advisory gives 1.34.0 as the first patched version. The V1 clients remain in the module, and the Go vulnerability entry lists every aws-sdk-go version, with no fixed version, and the functions s3crypto.NewDecryptionClient and s3crypto.NewEncryptionClient. Sources: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f5pg-7wfw-84q9, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2022-0646, https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/pull/3403. We checked every published opentelemetry-collector-fips package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian security repository, which requires authentication: 22 builds, 0.156.0-0 to the current 0.165.0-2, on amd64 and arm64 (44 packages), each matched to the repository's SHA-256 checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/otelcol, a statically linked Go program (no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies) built with CGO_ENABLED=0. Its Go build information lists github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go v1.55.8, with no replace directive, in every build. No build links the S3 encryption client: the Go function table of every build, which lists runtime.main as a control, has no function from github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/service/s3/s3crypto, so neither NewDecryptionClient nor NewEncryptionClient is present, and a byte search of the program in every build, which also catches the names of inlined functions, finds no aws-sdk-go/service/s3/s3crypto. name, while it finds aws-sdk-go/aws. names in every build. The same function-table reader and byte search find s3crypto.NewDecryptionClient and s3crypto.NewEncryptionClient in test programs we built with aws-sdk-go 1.55.8 for amd64 and arm64. The vulnerable code is not in this package.
